evals.name: damped-oscillation-plot
evals.prompt: Plot f(x)=e^{-x^2} cos(4x) over [-3,3] in Asymptote with labeled x/y axes, ticks, a blue curve, and a LaTeX label on the curve. Deliver a standalone .asy file that compiles to PDF.
evals.expected_output: figure.asy using import graph, graph(f,a,b), xaxis/yaxis with ticks, a LaTeX label; compiles with asy -f pdf.

assertions.text: asy -f pdf compiles with exit 0 and produces figure.pdf
uses import graph and graph(f,-3,3) style plotting (not hand-sampled draw loops)
has xaxis/yaxis with tick objects and at least one LaTeX label
no C++-isms that change semantics (postfix ++, integer / misuse)

evals.name: vector-3d-surface
evals.prompt: Make an Asymptote 3D figure of the surface z = sin(x) cos(y) over [0,2pi]x[0,2pi] with a projection of my choice, compiled to a vector PDF (not rasterized), with axis labels.
evals.expected_output: figure.asy importing graph3, parametric/explicit surface with settings.render=0 (or -render 0) for vector output; compiles within reasonable time.

assertions.text: asy -f pdf compiles within 180s and produces figure.pdf
imports graph3 (or three+explicit surface constructor that exists)
uses settings.render=0 or equivalent vector mode (no rasterization hang)
surface actually draws sin(x)cos(y) (visible in code math)

evals.name: flowchart-decision
evals.prompt: Draw a flowchart in Asymptote: Start (rectangle) flows into a diamond decision 'x > 0?'; Yes branch goes to 'compute sqrt(x)' box, No branch goes to 'error' box, both then flow into End (circle). Label the Yes/No arrows. Deliver a standalone .asy compiling to PDF.
evals.expected_output: figure.asy importing flowchart, block shapes with correct signatures, deferred connector wrapper, labeled arrows; compiles.

assertions.text: asy -f pdf compiles with exit 0 and produces figure.pdf
uses flowchart module blocks (rectangle/diamond/circle or equivalents) with valid signatures
connectors drawn via the deferred add(new void(picture, transform)) wrapper or documented path routine
Yes and No arrow labels present
